The model form, while providing a well-fit dataset should not be taken as truly indicative of underlying thermodynamics. It should be noted, that some of the papers provided expressions or alternate methods for boundary calculation rendering this read-off procedure unnecessary. The authors used the following procedure to “read off” values as accurately as possible. 1. Find the highest resolution picture of the phase diagram image possible. 2. Crop as tightly as possible to known tick marks. Typically lines are at least 3 pixels wide depending on image (source of error). Tilt makes the potential error worse. 3. Note the total x and y extent in real units as well as pixels. 4. Images count pixels from top left corner. 5. Far left starting point. Far right is 100% uranium for most (not all) phase diagrams 6. Threshold image, save as bitmap. 7. Trim line intersections to provide a 1 pixel separation. Lines that are very close together (typically solidus/liquidus close to the U-rich terminus) must be separated prior to intersection. 8. select each line, save xy coordinates to separate file 9. correction factors are in per pixel 10. Far left and lowest temperature of image are the x0 and y0 respectively. 11. The vertical number of pixels in the image is also used during correction. This is the denominator of the y correction factor. At time of this writing, not a separate named variable. 12. Import the xy coordinates and determine a fitted model 35 Appendix 3, Rate Assessment Plots A fitting methodology was used for distillation of several measurements made with a variety of heating or cooling rates. Here, we have determined the ideal value of the nucleation onset, the melting onset, and the observed endset of the melting reaction using their trends as a function of rate. The value of the line at 10 K/min (the rate at which the calibration is performed) was used as the rate independent point value. These were fit using a linear model weighted by the melting cycle. The vertical error associated with the solidus points are defined by the maximum and minimum values after applying the model parameter standard error. Weighting is according to Cycle−2 since the signal quality was found to decrease after repeated melting and solidification. 36 Figure 17: All of the fitted models used to incorporate different heating cooling rates into a determination of the best value for each composition and type of assessment point.
